title: Shard / hybrid orchestration
question: How does `mini-agent-rs orchestrate` split one coding task into many small jobs that run at the same time, and still end with code that builds?
summary: A coordinator written in ordinary code (no AI model planning) works out which files the task is about. It prepares ONE shared conversation (the whole repo plus the task) and starts one worker per file. Each worker is a copy of that conversation plus an instruction: change only your file. If a model call is slow, a backup copy of it starts and whichever good answer arrives first is used. A simple check sends suspicious answers back for another try. Files are saved as answers arrive, then the code is formatted and checked; if the check fails, only the files named in the error are repaired.
source: agent-rs/src at perf/hybrid-shard-clones 062b27f (PR #96); shard core merged in #94 and #95

responsibilities: A file is a target if the task names its path, or its topic word appears in the task
If nothing matches, every file is a target; the check fills any gap later
process: Wanted words = words of the task, minus the "do not touch" words.
A file is a target when the task quotes its path or one of its topic words is wanted.
All files are still shown to the model as background; only the number of workers shrinks (task t09: 20 → 4 workers).

process: Conversation = [role description, repo + task].
If the task does not spell out its contract, one model call writes it (names, function signatures, JSON field names, status codes) and it is added to the conversation.
The conversation is shared read-only by all worker threads (no copy per thread).

nodes.label: Work splitter
nodes.summary: One worker per file, or small balanced groups

attributes.name: max files per group
attributes.description: Tried 15: one file was missed in 7 of 8 calls

attributes.name: size of a file
attributes.description: The extra 400 covers the minimum cost of answering any file

responsibilities: Up to 2× the parallel-calls limit → one worker per file
More files → groups of neighbouring files, balanced by size, so all jobs fit in about one round of the rate limit
process: Files are taken in path order, so related files stay together (all types/*.ts, all components).
A group closes when its size passes total ÷ parallel calls, or when it reaches 6 files.
Each group runs on its own thread.

nodes.label: Backup calls (hedging)
nodes.summary: Copies race; the first good answer wins

attributes.name: max calls per job
attributes.description: The first call plus its backups

attributes.name: answer times
attributes.description: How long answers took in this round

attributes.name: backup delay when repairing
attributes.description: Used by the repair rounds

operations.name: when to start a backup
operations.description: The starting delay until ¼ of the round has answered (at least 3), then 2× the typical (median) time, kept between 1.5 s and the starting delay

responsibilities: Beat the provider's slow outliers (a 150-token answer that takes 20 s)
A failed or rejected answer starts a new copy right away
process: Takes a free slot and starts the first call.
Looks every 250 ms or less; when the newest call is older than the backup delay and a slot is free, starts a backup copy.
Good answer → records how long it took and returns it. Error or rejected → starts another copy, up to 8 calls.
Calls that lost the race simply free their slot when they finish.

nodes.label: Worker (copy of the conversation)

attributes.name: edit mode
attributes.description: First call on a file over 600 bytes: answer with search-and-replace edits; backups send the whole file

attributes.name: model settings
attributes.description: GLM: thinking off, no tools; backup calls get their own extra settings

responsibilities: Do not investigate, plan or review: just carry out the instruction
Use the task's names exactly (plural of <E> = name + s)
process: Copies the conversation and adds the instruction for its file(s), plus a note when a previous copy was rejected.
One file: edits (first call, file over 600 bytes) or the whole file between <<<FILE … FILE>>> markers. Several files: one block, or `UNCHANGED <path>`, per file.
If an edit cannot be applied, it counts as an error, and a backup copy answers with the whole file.

process: Retries "too many requests" (429) and server (5xx) errors, waiting a bit longer each time with some randomness, up to the limit in MINI_AGENT_RETRY_MAX_WAIT.
The provider caches the shared start of the conversation: extra workers mostly pay only for their instruction and answer.

attributes.name: copies that must pass

judge an answer

process: A rejected answer is reported as an error ("doubted: …"), so the backup mechanism starts the next copy, whose instruction includes the reason.
A wrong suspicion never blocks a file: after 5 copies, answers are accepted.
